verses.text: When the festival was over, the Israelites who had been there went out to the towns of Judah. They smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and altars throughout Judah and Benjamin, and also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had removed them all. Then they went back to their own towns and property.

Hezekiah assigned the priests and Levites to their divisions, each person with specific duties. They presented burnt offerings and peace offerings, served, gave thanks, and offered praise at the gates of the LORD's sanctuary.

The king set aside part of his own possessions for the daily morning and evening burnt offerings, and for those offered on Sabbaths, at new moons, and at the appointed festivals, as written in the LORD's law.
He ordered the people living in Jerusalem to give the priests and Levites their share so they could devote themselves to the LORD's law.

As soon as the order went out, the Israelites brought generous first portions of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and everything their fields produced. They brought in a tenth of all they had in great abundance.

The people of Israel and Judah who lived in Judah's towns also brought a tenth of their cattle and sheep and a tenth of what had been dedicated to the LORD their God. They piled the offerings in heaps.
They began making the piles in the third month and finished in the seventh.
When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps.

Azariah the chief priest, from Zadok's family, answered, "Ever since the people started bringing their offerings into the LORD's house, we've had enough to eat with plenty left over. The LORD has blessed his people, and this great supply is what remains."
Hezekiah ordered them to prepare storerooms in the LORD's house, and they did.
They faithfully brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated gifts. Conaniah the Levite was in charge, and his brother Shimei was his deputy.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were supervisors under Conaniah and his brother Shimei. King Hezekiah and Azariah, who was in charge of God's house, had appointed them.
Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the guard at the East Gate, was in charge of the voluntary offerings to God. He distributed the offerings made to the LORD and the most sacred gifts.
Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah served under him in the priests' towns. They were entrusted with giving each division of their fellow priests its share, whatever their rank.

This was in addition to the males three years old and up listed in the family records, including everyone who came into the LORD's house for daily service according to their divisions and assigned duties.
The priests were listed by family, and the Levites twenty years old and up were listed by division and responsibility.
The records also included their little ones, wives, sons, and daughters, everyone in the community. They faithfully kept themselves consecrated for their duties.
In every town, people were appointed by name to give shares to the male descendants of Aaron the priests living on their towns' pasturelands, and to everyone listed in the Levites' family records.
Hezekiah carried this out throughout Judah and did what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.
In everything he undertook to serve God's house and follow the law and commands, he sought his God wholeheartedly and succeeded.
